answer: Cedar Pearl Consensus Each agent must generate a unique cryptographic signature from a shared nebula of decentralized randomness. The signature is derived from both the agent’s public key and a time-bound challenge issued by the network. To maintain consistency, every agent must re-sign this challenge exactly once per epoch using their original key. Clones, unable to diverge due to identical key material, fail when required to produce distinct signatures under slightly different conditions—such as varying nonce seeds or timing jitter.
